### September 16 – October 7, 2026 — voxel editing moves from a direct chunk tool to semantic body edits, then loses terrain morphology

September 16's `2ce923f` adds the first playable voxel-editing loop: a built-in Voxel Hand raycasts one dense `VoxelChunk` and applies a spherical Add or Remove operation. Same-day `5efc021` and `65d4ea1` replace that single-cache assumption with a procedural base plus ordered sparse modifications, spatial edit indexing, and chunk rematerialization. This is a step toward reconstructible worlds; the word “authoritative” at this stage describes the in-memory base/edit model, not disk persistence or Workshop-authored terrain.

USF work starting September 22 adds another ownership level. `VoxelSemanticAuthority` stores edits in a body-local frame on the semantic body, while each Scale-Slice `VoxelScaleRealization` owns its derived dense cache. The October source retains both this shared semantic log and a standalone realization's inline `VoxelModificationLayer`; they serve different ownership contexts. On October 5, `e987230` removes earlier focused tests for chunk sampling, edits, modifications, worlds, streaming and base generation. Only two files in the current voxel tree contain inline tests; they cover realization-intent roles and demand-region planning rather than durable save/load, edit replay after restart, or cross-slice visual equivalence.

On October 7, `69780e1` removes 2,701 lines across 21 files, including the rocky/lunar profiles, terrain bands, cave fields and much of the GPU density path. The current celestial base is a sphere, with the Voxel Hand's analytic edits still applied to it in memory. This sequence is not a monotonic climb toward a finished terrain editor: it alternates between a working edit demonstration, stronger semantic/cache separation, test removal, and a major terrain-capability retreat. The current source has no serialization contract for these edit types or world save/load path; “persistent” means cache-durable within the live process. No runtime or save/reload test was performed. See the [current-state edit map](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#voxel-edits-survive-cache-rebuilding-but-are-not-durable-authored-saves) and [focused source/history review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--voxel-edit-authority-is-cache-durable-but-not-a-saved-world-format).


## October 23, 2026 — Rust Analyzer moved into named IDE modules, not into a frontend-neutral API

The IDE language-server workflow was already substantial before the extraction: [`220cc867`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-GUI/commit/220cc86785f77c8ba6f7e0722e22f3bdcc568c2d) adds a 1,120-line `language_server.rs`, with initialization, requests, buffer/version association and edit review now separated from the main UI module. Fifteen minutes later, [`80c654ca`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-GUI/commit/80c654ca0d629aba955328d774c68a589cad6d52) places text/position conversions and safe edit helpers in `lsp_text.rs`. These are meaningful responsibility-oriented file extractions, but they do not move LSP request semantics into Vapor's service: the Client service launches and bounds the pinned Rust Analyzer process, whereas the IDE still constructs requests, interprets most JSON-RPC and owns version-aware edits. The service's typed promotion is selective (`publishDiagnostics`); most remaining LSP messages cross as generic JSON.

The current path also shows intentional restraint around implicit work: Rust Analyzer options disable check-on-save, build scripts and proc macros. That is source evidence of selected side-effect controls, not proof that opening a workspace performs no Cargo metadata work or that all background CPU use is absent. The service maps one analyzer process per client connection, so parallel clients can duplicate analyzer instances for the same workspace; this implication has not been measured. The subsequent plan for semantic objects, diagnostics and editor integration is documented intent, not a completed shared semantic runtime. See the [latest-state IDE ownership analysis](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--rust-analyzer-runs-under-the-client-service-while-ide-semantics-remain-frontend-owned).

## July 23 – October 22, 2026 — server recovery grows around three databases, then deployment adds a fifth service

The Platform Server first acquires a root deploy script on July 23 ([`4872c51`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-Platform-Server/commit/4872c516150a5ca5a89b54564c0ee2d0824fc0e7)), then state export/restore that day ([`1088d56`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-Platform-Server/commit/1088d56f69c62c70f7ef79852cd40c90d5fe002e)) and a periodic export timer on July 24 ([`3ec87f6`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-Platform-Server/commit/3ec87f624c3379b3bc6afd248c15e07a315633c8)). Restore initially replaces the service state root after stopping the then-stateful Docs, Identity and Diagnostics services. July 25's [`a2a95925`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-Platform-Server/commit/a2a9592577ba2b568346d1ca6703f0bde8e72fb4) adds tar-member validation, schema/secrets markers and a small test suite; the same history also includes a malformed `state/`-as-file path that can fail after the live state root has been moved, already detailed in the source review.

On September 7, [`e9e4ba3`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-Platform-Server/commit/e9e4ba3678a1feb16cc60a86531a115765cd5ce7) adds Registry to the systemd units, build list, state/config setup and health check. This is a real deployed-service addition, but the older exporter and restore service arrays remain three entries. On October 22, [`d02a0c6a`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-Platform-Server/commit/d02a0c6acf083a00f06d62b35cff49852ed3cab1) records the intended Registry-catalog / Identity-authorization boundary, while [`a98770ad`](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Vapor-Platform-Server/commit/a98770ad290a02f2a03dc1519b9a66dd8b516f1c) advances the workspace-manifest shape. Neither reconciles Registry state into backup/restore. The operational-evidence document still describes only three state directories and was not updated with the new service.

A second ownership seam is visible in the lock design. The scheduled systemd deploy wraps the script with `flock`; exporter and restore take the same lock internally. The README also documents direct invocation of `deploy.sh`, which has no internal lock. Thus automated paths coordinate, while the supported manual path can bypass their mutual exclusion. This conclusion is source-derived; no overlapping jobs or recovery rehearsal was run. See the [current recovery cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#platform-server-operations-deploy-is-broader-than-its-recovery-boundary) and [detailed review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--platform-server-deployment-backup-and-restore-disagree-on-registry-ownership).

The pre-DNS ingress contract also changed after the only dated VPS verification. July's fallback Caddy block imported the Vapor routes under the temporary HTTP host. September 14's `b17c531` changes that same block to redirect every request to the canonical HTTPS domain, while the deployment README and Identity runbook retain direct HTTP-by-IP testing instructions. The last recorded VPS verification is July 25, so it cannot prove whether the changed redirect reached the VPS; source-level, it removes direct pre-DNS service access. The root `public-http-check.sh` expects direct status codes, and the GitHub smoke does not follow redirects and later expects exact `401`, so neither can certify the redirected host as healthy. No live request was made. See the [operator access/ingress map](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#platform-server-operator-access-and-http-ingress-map).


## October 21–22, 2026 — GUI primitives emerge from product-specific work

The Rust IDE workbench added a shared syntax-colored editor and searchable workspace tree (`78d5da0`). The following day, the Launcher/authoring console was extracted into a common model (`dab912c`), and a compact reusable Panel was added while Launcher’s lifecycle views were substantially reorganized (`2360437`). The current-state audit finds these components are useful but not uniformly adopted: Launcher consumes Panel, IDE consumes editor/tree, and Studio’s inspected views retain their own presentation paths. This chronology suggests the toolkit grew opportunistically at the seam where each product needed a widget, rather than through one explicit design-system and preview workflow. It is a source-backed interpretation of the commit order and current callsites, not a claim about the original authors’ unrecorded motives. See the [shared GUI core review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--the-shared-gui-core-is-real-but-its-design-system-reach-is-uneven).
### October 2–6, 2026 — Developer Lab presets become a small overlay over typed runtime variables

October 2 `05f5a55` adds a 429-line Developer Lab module: one `freecam` preset, commands to list/apply/clear presets, and a status command. The design captures pre-application values, applies through existing runtime-variable setters, supports ordered overlapping assignments, and attempts to restore snapshots after setter failure. Two tests only check active-name ordering and that a preset can be inserted into the registry. October 5 `e987230` removes those tests while the module is still monolithic. On October 6 `ab65b8e` extracts command, model, and transaction responsibilities into separate files; `0e48843` adds a module map. Current code still registers only freecam, preserves direct runtime-variable editing alongside the recorded preset stack, and has no persistence contract. The history therefore records a useful adapter/composition layer, not a general user-authored preset system or exclusive settings owner. See the [current implementation review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--developer-lab-presets-are-reversible-runtime-variable-overlays-not-an-exclusive-configuration-owner) and [current-state cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#october-26--developer-lab-composes-local-runtime-variables-without-owning-them).
### September 13 – October 6, 2026 — World Draw makes spatial diagnostics reusable and keeps text in inspection

The developer-tools redesign's September 13 `64ca5e9` adds a 748-line World Draw stack for reusable spatial colors, primitives, scalar fields, and their renderer. The following `625fd2e` “Stage 3B” pass deliberately removes functionality that did not belong in world geometry: draw payloads stay spatial; text, labels, legends and linguistic/numeric detail belong to developer inspection/UI. This makes visualization a reusable data/render boundary rather than a per-feature debug mesh API. October 6 `0e48843` reorganizes the implementation into color, frame, primitive-render and scalar-field-render modules. The current design retains the shared frame/batch bus and producer-versus-renderer split. Its present costs and extension limits are implementation-level: scalar meshes rebuild when submitted each frame, absent IDs are hidden but not reclaimed, IDs are frame-unique static strings, and exported descriptors are not fully validated. No runtime or profile evidence establishes whether those limits matter at current scale. See the [current implementation analysis](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--world-draw-is-a-reusable-spatial-snapshot-api-with-a-cached-mesh-path-that-rebuilds-every-collected-frame) and [current-state cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#october-26--world-draw-is-a-frame-scoped-geometry-bus-not-a-retained-or-validated-visualization-model).

### September 19–20, 2026 — input focus becomes one shared manual-claim resource

September 19 `473314b` introduces `InputFocus` as a generic `HashSet` of static owner IDs split into pointer and gameplay claims. Its stated aim is to let tools and UI declare temporary ownership while concrete adapters decide how that affects cursor/gameplay input. September 20 `52d13eb` adds a monotonic gameplay-resume epoch; the player cursor adapter uses that edge to restore persistent capture intent after modal dismissal without treating the modal as the owner of the player's preference. Later console, world-selection, developer-palette, creative-menu, editor-shell and gizmo integrations reuse this one resource. The cross-cutting convenience is real, but each producer must balance its own string claim, no priority/winner or scoped lifetime is recorded, and consumers cannot explain which owner currently blocks input. This documents the implementation's simplicity and its ownership tradeoff, not a reported input bug. See the [focused source review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--input-focus-is-a-shared-set-of-manual-claims-not-a-lease-or-priority-arbiter) and [current-state cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#input-focus-centralizes-blocking-but-claims-remain-manually-balanced-strings).

### September 19–23, 2026 — a small view contract centralizes viewport coordinates, then adds presentation policy

September 19 `473314b` introduces the primary-view marker, immersive/embedded presentation state, `ViewRay`, and camera logical-viewport conversions in one 118-line module. September 23 `8f3eb98` adds a view-subject presentation marker so self-visibility can remain a view concern; `baf3e95` adds the dedicated USF presentation layer and records that it uses the semantic observer origin rather than cockpit/boom camera offsets. The current editor shell assigns the game camera a tab viewport while cursor/gizmo consumers share coordinate conversion. This is a concrete common seam, but it remains a singular primary-view abstraction with global presentation state; the later multi-entry USF demand snapshot is a separate, broader observer model. October 6 `0e48843` makes only a whitespace cleanup in this module. See the [current view contract review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--view-helpers-centralize-viewport-coordinates-while-the-product-state-remains-one-global-primary-view) and [cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#view-coordinate-contract-is-shared-but-primary-presentation-state-is-singular).
### September 12 – October 6, 2026 — character movement intent and contact state gain explicit ownership

The September 12 rename-era `83f20d9` establishes a standalone character-physics domain: immutable movement configuration, a keyboard/camera-independent input component, movement math, runtime contact state, plugin, and controller. `6eb90b2` adds `speed_multiplier` to the input contract so sprint/crouch-like adapters can adjust movement intent without rewriting tuning policy. September 24 `e2b9282` makes the central invariant change: public `grounded`, `ground_entity`, and `ground_normal` fields become one private optional `CharacterGroundContact`; groundedness is derived from contact presence, and transition changes move behind explicit methods. This prevents public contradictory contact tuples and centralizes tick edges, jump, clear, and topology invalidation. October 6 `0e48843` renames input to intent and divides motor implementation into grounding, movement, stepping, and pushing modules while preserving one ordered fixed-tick orchestrator. The evolution is from a generic controller toward explicit state invariants and decomposed mechanics; it still relies on adapters respecting public intent fields and on the controller sequence remaining coherent. No physics tests were run. See [current motor review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--character-motor-separates-device-intent-contact-truth-and-fixed-tick-integration) and [current-state cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#character-movement-has-three-frame-owners-with-different-update-cadences).
### September 12 – October 5, 2026 — character movement profile is explicit but its focused tests are removed

The September 12 character-physics extraction places Source/Quake-derived acceleration, capped air wish behavior, friction, dimensional hulls, and SI-labelled movement settings behind reusable math/config modules. The profile itself documents intentional departures from Source 2013—stronger ground friction and a higher jump—so `source_2013` records lineage, not parity. Earlier focused tests expressed four math invariants (wish-speed bound, friction cannot reverse, air cap limits parallel gain, axis rejection) and two conversion checks (Earth gravity response and speed/jump preservation at a nonzero chart). October 5 `e987230` deletes those tests along with frame tests, 113 lines total. Current source keeps conversion for length-like values and gravity while acceleration/friction coefficients stay authored; whether this preserves desired movement feel across charts is not resolved by the removed tests. The deletion is a verified regression in local regression coverage, not evidence that the equations currently fail. See [current math/config review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--character-movement-math-is-quake-derived-with-chart-conversion-only-for-selected-quantities) and [cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#character-math-and-tuning-are-si-labelled-but-only-partially-chart-verified).
### September 13–19, 2026 — character observability becomes an opt-in shared developer visualization

The character motor's early `observability.rs` file is renamed `devtools.rs` in the September 13 developer-tools redesign (`78082f4`) and moved into a folder module during the September 19 cleanup (`473314b`). The current collector registers a default-disabled `physics.character` visualization through shared DevTools, then emits velocity/up/contact-normal arrows through World Draw. This replaces a feature-local observability name with the common developer visualization vocabulary, while keeping only a few spatial signals; the current source does not turn it into a telemetry inspector. The shared host is registered by the DevTools plugin rather than CharacterMovementPlugin, so it is an optional cross-plugin integration. No rendered output was assessed. See the [current character visualization review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--character-physics-is-generic-by-contract-while-its-debug-view-is-opt-in-and-shallow) and [cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#character-physics-is-generic-by-contract-but-its-debug-view-is-opt-in-and-shallow).
### September 14–October 6, 2026 — semantic inspection evolves from editor selection into typed, authority-aware data

September 14–15 editor/gizmo work establishes semantic inspection beside raw ECS inspection. Commit 06e9b72 states the strongest written contract: inspection frames are renderer-independent snapshots; direct, validated, transactional and command access are distinct; edits and actions return to domain owners; and raw reflection is not semantic meaning. The same design describes an egui widget layer intended for multiple hosts and uses Thermal as a second domain proof. September 19 adds derive-based Inspect metadata, explicit type registration and semantic sections; September 20 adds domain-owned thermal request handling. By October 6, source modules split the model, metadata, registry, traversal traits and frame protocol. The core remains inside Bevy: frames/messages and targets use Bevy entities, so the model is presentation-independent but not a cross-process Vapor service API ([September design commit](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/06e9b72a), [current inspection module](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/mod.rs>), [frame protocol](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/frame/mod.rs>), [metadata](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/metadata/mod.rs>), [type registry](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/registry/mod.rs>)).

There is a sharp evidence reversal on October 5–6. Commit e987230 deletes the 80-line derive/mutability test that asserted skipped fields stay hidden and only Direct fields reach mutable visitors; no replacement remains in the current tree. On October 6, 0e48843 deletes the architecture and roadmap documents that held detailed inspector, gizmo and editor invariants. The current implementation still reflects some of those choices, but the same-week document deletion and test removal make history less discoverable and leave the authority contract less regression-protected. The immersive view is text-only Bevy UI while the embedded editor uses egui, and duplicate section IDs panic. These are current limitations/evidence gaps; the deleted test was not rerun ([removed derive test](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/e987230f240378353fe7afe1f5508649e318252b), [architecture/roadmap deletion](https://github.com/GHF-Studios/Loo-Cast/commit/0e488433dd26b35a937dba8c5f755b52615e8eaf), [screen inspector](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/ui/inspector/mod.rs>), [inspection model](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/model/mod.rs>), [traversal rules](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/devtools/inspect/traits/mod.rs>)).

### September 28–29, 2026 — collision queries progress from observation contract to flight motion gate

`295362f` introduces canonical swept-collision contracts around one semantic SI motion segment. Its key architectural decision is explicit: Scale-Slice and local representations may report conservative evidence, but they do not own impulse/response authority. `1d868d8` adds revision-scoped per-frame requests and candidate records, initially documenting the frame as observation-only while the eventual prepare → providers/refinement → accept → commit transaction remains future work. Later September 29 `93b1a2a` improves floating-origin backend updates for Avian; this is a separate representation-coherence path, not a collision provider. October 6 module extraction reorganizes the query contracts, frame, and provider runtime. October 9 `46e1eac` connects the query transaction to canonical flight: prepare proposes a sweep, the voxel provider answers, and flight waits for finalization before committing. Current code therefore completes more than the original observation surface, but the installed provider remains voxel semantic geometry only, and its advertised lookahead is not consumed. It has no located focused tests or runtime evidence in this audit. The user's later Moon-braking report is not established as a defect in this mechanism. See the [current collision-query review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--canonical-collision-queries-are-wired-into-flight-but-demand-and-provider-coverage-are-partial) and [current-state cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#canonical-collision-sweeps-protect-kinematic-flight-with-a-voxel-only-provider).


### September 26 – October 6, 2026 — USF chart algebra separates from runtime rebase; granularity policy moves into Spatial

September 26 `569c781` introduces pure `UsfChart` projection over canonical position. September 27 `f13b31c` adds a scale-tagged `UsfChartDelta`, which makes floating-origin displacement convertible across resident Scale Slices. October 6 `0e48843` places the runtime chart state and ECS rebase schedule under `spatial/chart`, leaving numeric projection under `usf/chart`; root transforms, Avian positions and collider leaves are preflighted before a single origin shift is applied and announced. In parallel, October 2 `cb094c1` first adds the realization-granularity policy request; October 6 moves it to a public Spatial module. Its one current voxel caller consumes only the validity horizon while fixing resolution to one chunk, and extreme finite inputs can overflow intermediate/output values. The split chart ownership is coherent in source; the solver's generality and numeric guarantees are less settled. No runtime or boundary testing is claimed. See [current-state cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#usf-charts-runtime-rebase-and-realization-granularity-have-distinct-owners) and [focused source review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--scale-local-granularity-is-bounded-by-policy-but-the-public-solver-can-still-emit-infinity).


### October 7–8, 2026 — canonical voxel sampling is reduced to a spherical field adapter

`69780e1` removes the previous terrain profiles, bands, caves and GPU density path, replacing the active celestial field with a sphere; the current `CelestialVoxelField` stores radius plus a coarsest detail scale and samples the same radial signed-distance field through bounded local charts. October 8 restructures the prepared sampler into field/sampling modules, preserving the scale-independent field but not the removed authoring capabilities. If canonical preparation fails, the current fallback returns empty terrain instead of a typed generation error; this is a conditional source behavior, not an observed fixture failure. Core materialization identity now uses checked 64-bit canonical offsets, but the older hidden `VoxelChunkCoord` adapter still exposes unchecked `IVec3 * 10`. See [focused review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--celestial-dense-sampling-is-a-bounded-sphere-adapter-but-failed-coordinate-preparation-becomes-empty-terrain) and [cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#celestial-sampling-preserves-one-spherical-field-across-scales-but-failure-falls-back-to-empty).

### October 9, 2026 — voxel collision adds a canonical SDF narrow phase separate from local trimeshes

Commit `46e1eac` adds bounded body-local SI tracing over the celestial sphere plus semantic Add/Remove edit geometry. The provider broad-phases candidate intervals and treats incomplete or exhausted traces as `Unknown`, so high-speed collision no longer depends on whether dense chunks or local Avian colliders happen to be resident. The material path remains separately derived from Surface Nets and filters rigid triangles by `VoxelCollisionMode`. Current code does not preserve that policy in the narrow phase: it drops Add material identity, ignores Paint, and thus treats the Voxel Hand's Control-added non-rigid NEBULA as blocking despite the trimesh path excluding non-rigid material. Each query also repeats broad-phase collection for candidate publication and resolution, then scans all edits per candidate/sample; the authority has no source-level spatial index. These are confirmed source differences and complexity, not runtime findings or evidence for the Moon braking report. See [focused collision review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--semantic-voxel-sweeps-and-rigid-material-collision-disagree-for-non-rigid-edits) and [cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#voxel-collision-queries-disagree-with-rigid-material-policy-and-repeat-edit-work).

### October 26, 2026 — position precision review separates intentional finite-world wrap from open coarsening semantics

The current Scale Stack explicitly has 71 decimal spatial slices, a finite top-scale root, and balanced carries whose top winding is discarded. The October 9 USF spatial-authority plan retains that range; current arithmetic comments intentionally define root wrap. This is recorded as an actual domain choice, not an assumed bug. The unresolved precision boundary is the `f32` leaf: coarsening `UsfPosition` folds finer digits into a parent residual, and a callsite sweep finds that result used both for scale-local projection and for materialization address selection. The old 23 focused USF tests included tolerance-based re-expression and mixed-precision checks, but October 5 `e987230` removed them without a current equivalent. That establishes lost regression evidence and an untyped quantization boundary; it does not establish a reproduced voxel misaddress. See [current-state cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#canonical-coordinates-and-scale-local-projections-do-not-share-one-precision-contract), [focused position review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#canonical-position-arithmetic-hierarchical-identity-with-a-bounded-float-leaf), and [callsite follow-up](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#follow-up--lossy-scale-re-expression-has-callers-with-different-semantic-needs).


### October 6, 2026 — moving semantic orientation joins canonical position and velocity, while a kinematic snapshot remains unused

The celestial-motion work introduces orientation-only `UsfSemanticFrame` alongside canonical `UsfPosition` and SI `UsfCanonicalMotion`; world position is not duplicated inside the frame. The October 6 Spatial reorganization also exports a `UsfKinematicFrameState` value that combines origin, frame and motion, but current repository search finds no consumer beyond its declaration and re-export. This is a useful marker of a boundary that exists in types but not yet in runtime behavior. Later locomotion uses per-step f32 displacement error to choose runtime versus canonical motion; the handoff saturates projected velocity independently, so displacement readiness alone does not guarantee lossless velocity authority. The current orientation math also has finite-extreme normalization gaps. These findings qualify the integration claim without asserting a normal-play failure. See [focused semantic-frame/motion review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--semantic-frames-validate-orientation-weakly-runtime-eligibility-checks-displacement-but-not-velocity-projection) and [current cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#semantic-frame-orientation-and-motion-handoff-have-numeric-contracts-beyond-displacement).


### September 21–October 26, 2026 — travel influence, semantic boundary and physical contact remain separate geometry paths

September 21 `d559e3e6` adds scale-aware travel influences so navigation pace can respond to world structure rather than a fixed body-radius floor. September 27 `0e46041f` adds a reusable travel-boundary resolver for hard bodies. The October 6 Spatial reorganization puts that generic provider contract under `spatial/navigation`; the later volumetric projection work adds nearest-zero-crossing geometry for voxel demand/contact. At the October 26 source snapshot, the current celestial fixture is still a sphere, so radial navigation and volumetric contact samples agree. The connection is conditional: navigation's `CelestialVoxelField::sample_near` still delegates to radial `surface_near`, while voxel contact preparation calls `boundary_near` on the canonical field. If cave or non-radial geometry returns, travel clearance and contact-demand anchoring can disagree until the navigation adapter switches to the full field boundary. The evidence establishes an integration seam and current sphere-only behavior, not a runtime collision/braking defect. See [focused spatial-navigation review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--spatial-navigation-has-bounded-measurements-but-context-priority-and-boundary-refinement-remain-coarse) and [current-state cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#spatial-navigation-derives-a-bounded-context-from-a-global-influence-scan).


### September 22–October 26, 2026 — Scale Slices are persistent runtime partitions with a separate debug view

September 22 `9de6680` expands the early spatial layer into a multiscale runtime with refinement and transition policy. By the October 26 snapshot, the `spatial/slice` model names 71 persistent roots and represents membership twice: a scale tag for hot-path systems and an ECS relationship for semantic navigation. October 6 `0e48843` renames the earlier `UsfChartMask` to `UsfScaleSliceMask`, clarifying that the bitset represents partition membership rather than projection math. The September 19 developer-tools cleanup `da6c985` had already extracted the spatial panel and demand visualization into their own modules. This arrangement preserves the distinction between runtime slice identity, view scale and realized capability, while introducing a synchronization obligation between the scale tag and relationship.

October 5 `e987230` removes two `UsfChartMask` tests: one checked that every supported scale occupied one unique bit and the union equalled `ALL`; the other checked inclusive-range order independence and membership. The current implementation keeps the corresponding operations under the renamed type, but the inspected source has no replacement tests. The deletion is evidence of reduced regression coverage, not a demonstrated mask defect. Current review also finds the demand debug renderer projects centers in shared-leaf native units but draws unconverted half-extents authored in each scope scale, so its cross-scale geometry does not preserve one coordinate chart; this visual finding is source-derived and not runtime-rendered. See [focused Scale Slice review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--scale-slices-are-semantic-partitions-but-their-debug-geometry-mixes-coordinate-units) and [current-state cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#scale-slices-separate-partition-identity-from-local-representation).

### October 2–8, 2026 — Voxel presentation shells and clip materials are separated from physical authority

The current manifestation layer treats ECS entities as disposable presentation shells: semantic materialization remains store-backed, while collision aggregation and capability coverage have separate owners. The frontier is rebuilt from coverage revisions and same-scale six-neighbor checks; it selects exposed coarse/fine faces for rendering but does not establish collision readiness. Retirement hides removed realization roots, reuses up to 512 shells, and despawns overflow. The material path compacts compatible cells into clip boxes, projects them through the view, and lets a WGSL shader cut apertures in the parent presentation. This makes the visual boundary more scalable than one shader entry per fine cell while leaving physical authority out of the renderer.

The lineage also shows incomplete cleanup. `a91c670` added Tracy manifestation-pressure counters; `eaef138` removed the counter/plot owner under profiler decontamination but left empty inline `record_*` methods and their rebuild call sites. October 5 `e987230` removed focused tests for pool reuse, refinement presentation policy and runtime pose update; the inspected current subtree contains no replacements for frontier, compaction, pooling or clip synchronization. On October 8 `d806e3d` split the accumulated material implementation into `asset`, `clip` and `systems` modules, clarifying file ownership without restoring the removed checks or observability. These are source/history findings, not a claim of a rendering or collision runtime failure. See the [current-state manifestation cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#voxel-manifestations-are-disposable-presentation-while-collision-and-coverage-have-separate-owners) and [focused review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--voxel-manifestation-cleanly-splits-presentation-from-physical-authority-with-deferred-retirement-and-stale-profiling-hooks).

### October 1–8, 2026 — voxel demand shifts from dense bounds to predictive, ranked work

`d8f0e3a` introduces incremental entering/leaving slab updates for a moving residency window. `ab65b8e` later makes the optimization stationary-only: predictive movement selects a sparse tube inside the swept AABB, so retaining the old AABB overlap is not equivalent to retaining the newly demanded tube. Motion now informs a bounded lookahead, candidate trajectory score and capability-aware work rank; it does not alter semantic movement authority. `eb6814f` adds view-frustum plus celestial surface-shell culling for view-owned regions, with an octant test for shell coverage.

On October 5, `e987230` removes focused checks for adaptive budget behavior, bounded moving-window hysteresis, high-speed forward preference, stationary ordering/cross-section, predictive horizon and disjoint jumps. `f588206` removes the older pinned-shell residency input and planner branches, leaving source/view scopes as the explicit work contract; later view-shell culling is a distinct view-owned path, not restoration of pinning. By the current snapshot, desired-set rank is capability-first, predictive tubes prioritize a rounded centerline plus six-neighbor expansion, and warm inactive residency is bounded. But the nominal 65,536 chunk limit truncates the retained final set rather than every intermediate traversal; predictive scopes are also processed in input order before their shared candidate set is globally ranked. Focus/rank inputs are more continuous than the discrete plan key, so an unchanged chunk key can preserve stale queue scores. The code demonstrates these bounds and ordering gaps; the audit has not measured a pathological runtime workload. See the [current-state cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#voxel-streaming-uses-predictive-priority-but-the-desired-work-bound-is-not-an-enumeration-bound) and [focused review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--voxel-demand-is-priority-aware-but-planner-bounds-and-rank-invalidation-are-incomplete).

The voxel work pool grew from one large module into an explicit facility with lanes, critical/normal priority, per-lane admission, worker-owned compute leases, cancellable publication tickets and pressure telemetry. The old implementation included tests for worker sizing, critical preemption and bounded bursts, independent capacity, and compute-lease lifetime; `e987230` removed those checks, while `d806e3d` on October 8 split the 600-line module into `executor`, `admission`, `queue`, `ticket` and `profiling` files without restoring tests. ### September 19–October 6, 2026 — materialization storage becomes an address-keyed hot/warm state machine

The store evolved from a direct chunk cache into the owner of active dense truth, warm inactive residency, derived surfaces and token-checked generation. `48f6002` and `8bea1d6` belong to the cache/delta performance phase; `e7efce5` adds asynchronous generation state, and `e987230` adds explicit failed reservations while removing the then-existing uniform-result store test. `0e48843` completes a substantial type/revision cleanup around dense materializations and derived surfaces. The intended boundary is clear in current comments: canonical keys and semantic edits outlive ECS shells; inactive dense data is disposable warm cache; derived surfaces are revision-bound products. One consequence of the address-only LRU is that reactivation does not invalidate prior queue nodes, so repeated reactivation can evict a recently reused entry ahead of older inactive data. No test or runtime measurement currently covers this. See [store review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--the-materialization-store-separates-semantic-residency-from-disposable-caches-but-its-warm-lru-is-keyed-only-by-address) and [cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#voxel-materialization-store-separates-canonical-residency-from-derived-and-render-caches).

### September 30–October 26, 2026 — generation becomes asynchronous and globally scheduled, with publication as another authority boundary

The generation path evolves from per-world background builds into immutable per-chunk recipes, scoped batching, globally bounded worker lanes, per-key reservation tokens and round-robin world scheduling. `e7efce5` changes batch and publication flow; `d8f0e3a` adds the entering/leaving residency optimization; `0e48843` later reorganizes worker-capacity scheduling and per-world ranking. Collision/editing jobs use critical admission, presentation jobs are single-chunk latency-sensitive batches, and background throughput work may group aligned chunks. Generation scope is only a processing grouping; runtime surfaces and collision retain chunk identity. Current source catches up authority edits at publication and checks tokens so retired jobs cannot resurrect data.

The async boundary has independent budgets: worker capacity, per-world generation chunk quota, maximum chunks per task, frame-level generated-materialization publication count and the shared reconstructible Publication budget. Completed tasks are currently published in entity-query order without carrying criticality into the task; one ready batch can consume the frame budget before a later critical result. Also, the batcher drops a popped key if its processing scope cannot be derived, and publication drops a completed result on address-conversion failure without releasing/failing its token. If either conditional conversion error occurs on active work, the unchanged plan may not enqueue it again. This is derived from current source state; no error path or saturated publication schedule was executed. See the [current cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#voxel-generation-has-stale-token-protection-but-publication-order-and-error-recovery-are-incomplete) and [focused review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--generation-has-bounded-publication-but-failure-paths-can-strand-active-work).

### September 12–October 6, 2026 — authored geometry becomes a generic asset pipeline, then loses its local validation/compile tests

The September geometry work establishes an authorable `.spacemap` RON format for generic primitives, parametric repetitions, markers, simple lights and kinematic motion. Its explicit goal is to keep engine geometry reusable and let scenario/game code supply meaning: the physics campus's `player_spawn` and portal markers are interpreted by the playground adapter, not by the geometry compiler. The subsystem separates schema/validation, compilation to a small intermediate representation, mesh/collider realization and hot-reload reconciliation. This is an early concrete example of the later desired content-vs-capability boundary, though it is a built-in Bevy asset pipeline rather than Vapor-managed content ([format and authoring intent](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/assets/maps/README.md>), [schema](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/asset/schema/mod.rs>), [plugin](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/mod.rs>), [runtime scene adapter](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/geometry/runtime/mod.rs>), [playground marker interpretation](</home/leslieghf/Vapor/Loo-Cast/spacetime-engine/src/game/playground/map/mod.rs>)).

The validation/compiler path initially had focused tests for schema rejection and generated geometry. On October 5, `e987230` removed those test modules; on October 6, `ab65b8e` split the large validation and compile modules into dedicated constraint, per-definition, map-wide, object-dispatch and IR files. The structural change improves local ownership, but the test deletion left the changed owners without replacement numerical or generation-budget oracles. Current inspection found a mismatch between floor-based sweep counting and quarter-increment tolerant compilation, plus an `f32` accumulator that can stop progressing on accepted input and keep a generator loop alive indefinitely. Those are findings from current source; no reproducer was executed. The schema loader also reads whole files without an explicit byte cap, and direct insertion of the public schema type can bypass loader validation. ### September 2026 — portal splitting moves from one large file to explicit physical adapters

The portal work begins as a gameplay-owned subsystem. Cleanup part 4 (`473314b`) changes its file layout into `mod.rs` directories without changing behavior. Cleanup part 6 (`6a0f6b7`) then extracts the 827-line rigid splitter into peer materialization, preparation, solver, character-contact and crossing/completion reconciliation modules, and extracts the 701-line shared splitter into aperture policy, candidate selection and a character lifecycle. This makes the division between shared aperture policy, kinematic character behavior and Avian dynamic-body behavior inspectable. Cleanup part 16 (`eaf0454`) moves the portal subsystem from `game/portal` to engine-root `portal`, while leaving portal-gun and playground usage in game code. The reorganization makes an implicit dependency visible: portal traversal and collision topology are engine capabilities, while the game supplies the player-facing tool and scenario.

The current implementation retains that split and adds a public command boundary for persistent endpoint placement/removal, pair support validation and collision-stencil activation. Rigid-body splitting attaches a temporary USF sibling realization to a reserved Avian peer; canonical spatial transitions retire that temporary state. The split is not a general arbitrary-authority manifestation mechanism. The shared predictor uses constant current linear velocity and static orientation over one tick, and active endpoint links are not rechecked after activation if another system mutates the public destination field. On October 5, `e987230` removed the portal topology tests for crossing direction/side, crossing fraction and inverse mapping; the current source has no focused replacements. No runtime physics proof is available from this audit. See the [portal source review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--portal-splitting-shares-candidate-policy-while-character-and-rigid-solver-adapters-retain-different-motion-authority) and [current-state cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#portal-splitting-shares-candidate-policy-but-character-movement-and-rigid-contacts-use-distinct-adapters).

One current lifecycle mismatch sits beneath the module split: rigid preparation restores the authority collider when a solver peer disappears, but character materialization skips restoration when its peer is missing or its source transform no longer yields a plane. Thus the cleanup split is not yet symmetric across the two adapters. This is a source-confirmed conditional stale-collider path, not a reproduced gameplay failure. Character remainder movement also uses four fixed `MoveAndSlide` subdivisions; the code bounds the loop but does not demonstrate that this is sufficiently accurate for arbitrary speed or obstacle thickness. The audit did not execute convergence or high-speed tests. The portal adapter analysis and missing historical test coverage are detailed in the [semantic review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--portal-splitting-shares-candidate-policy-while-character-and-rigid-solver-adapters-retain-different-motion-authority) and [current-state cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#portal-splitting-shares-candidate-policy-but-character-movement-and-rigid-contacts-use-distinct-adapters).

The presentation tree follows the same decomposition: directed portal faces receive path-specific render layers, images, materials and derived cameras. The depth limit is four, trees are built once during Startup, and target sizes track the primary game viewport so an embedded view can resize independently of its host window. Runtime configuration is not uniformly live: render scale is consumed during resize, but changing recursion depth or sidedness does not rebuild startup-created faces and cameras. The current render architecture and its open runtime-reconfiguration boundary are detailed in the [semantic review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--portal-splitting-shares-candidate-policy-while-character-and-rigid-solver-adapters-retain-different-motion-authority) and [cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#portal-splitting-shares-candidate-policy-but-character-movement-and-rigid-contacts-use-distinct-adapters). No GPU/runtime image inspection was conducted.

The split's numerical policy is also visible: oriented box support is projected into the aperture's two in-plane axes, the center crossing fraction is epsilon-guarded, and character crossing maps the interpolated pose/control frame before simulating the remaining tick. Contact with dynamic bodies uses the engine's existing kinematic-character effective-mass estimate and delta-speed cap, mapping impulses through the peer portal; this is a game-response bridge, not a symmetric solver coupling. The distinction matters when interpreting “physically coherent”: the rigid body peer participates in Avian constraints, while character peer contacts are manually bridged. The traveler type documents that its reserved solver peer is an implementation adapter, not authority identity. Current source details are in the [cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#portal-splitting-shares-candidate-policy-but-character-movement-and-rigid-contacts-use-distinct-adapters); portal-local checks remain absent after the ordinary crossing/mapping tests were deleted.

The September playground items show the engine/game seam in practice: item plugins register their own action metadata and emit portal, weapon, thermal or voxel-domain messages, while one gameplay adapter owns device bindings and aim. Damageable and chunk-demand cubes are game-side compositions of health/thermal/physics/USF/demand behavior, not yet Vapor content definitions. The USF graph now gives semantic roots linked-spawn ownership of authority partitions and logical realizations, but the split cube's disabled solver peer only enters that graph during active portal splitting. Root erase/death can therefore leave an inactive peer ECS entity behind. This derives from the present relationship/lifecycle code and has not been runtime-tested. See the [playground review](loo-cast-vapor-semantic-diff-review.md#october-26--playground-semantics-route-item-actions-cleanly-but-one-split-peer-lifetime-is-not-owned) and its [cross-reference](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#playground-semantics-route-item-actions-cleanly-but-one-split-peer-lifetime-is-not-owned).



### October 26 — Installed App identity and authored Workspace identity are confirmed as separate roots

Current installation code validates `App.vapor.toml` and derives the installation from `VAPOR_HOME` or the executable under `bin/`; the developer SDK's `Workspace.vapor.toml` discovery is a separate CWD-oriented operation. This is the intended correction to the reported Windows installer complaint: an installed Steam app root should be an App Instance, not an authored Vapor workspace. Base setup initializes user state and a canonical Superworkspace; role promotion then reconciles tools before persisting the role. However, Installer still performs base setup directly and role reconciliation through the shared service, leaving the full first-launch flow split across owners. The core uninstaller has transaction-style preflight and explicit external-data/source purge flags, while the current Installer UI exposes only default non-destructive uninstall. Windows GNU installs a gnullvm PATH folder, but its uninstall cleanup only removes the MSVC folder when built for MSVC. See the full [current installation/role/uninstall cross-check](current-state-semantic-cross-reference.md#installation-role-and-uninstall-data-ownership-is-explicit-but-the-ui-and-host-integration-do-not-fully-express-it); the source contract was inspected without running setup or uninstall.

Diagnostics began July 23 with an explicit service brief (`14e1381`), then gained a minimal binary (`b72ca78`), Axum migration and `target/` ignore (`7e08c42`), public status (`fb318fa`), report-v2 validation/redaction/quota (`058c403`), and the collapsed report API (`6a39a81`). The important continuity is the gap between declared lifecycle and delivered lifecycle. The original service concept already included durable diagnostics and authorized developer retrieval. Subsequent documentation calls for export/import and retention, while current routes only upload, list, retrieve one run, and export metadata. Quota is a refusal threshold, not retention. The historical sequence shows an intentionally narrow first vertical slice that was never fully brought back into line with its scope docs; it does not show those promises being explicitly withdrawn.
